node.title: Re: match two files
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
Although overkill for the example you showed, it might be useful to see how this can be done with SQL. The following uses [mod://DBD::CSV] so it can work with your input files directly to produce your expected output, though for "production" work you would probably want to use a real database. Also, my output code is somewhat simplistic, one could use [mod://Text::CSV]([mod://Text::CSV_XS|_XS]) for that purpose as well.

use warnings; use strict; use DBI; my $dbh = DBI->connect("dbi:CSV:", undef, undef, { csv_sep_char => "\t", f_ext => '', RaiseError => 1, }) or die "Cannot connect: $DBI::errstr"; my $sth = $dbh->prepare(<<'ENDSQL'); SELECT tmp01.PeptideID as PeptideID, tmp01.ProteinID as ProteinID, tmp02.SpectrumID as SpectrumID, tmp02.Sequence as Sequence FROM tmp01 LEFT OUTER JOIN tmp02 ON tmp01.PeptideID = tmp02.PeptideID ENDSQL $sth->execute; print join("\t", @{ $sth->{NAME} } ), "\n"; while ( my $row = $sth->fetchrow_arrayref ) { print join("\t", @$row ), "\n"; }

Update: Also make sure to read up on the different kinds of [wp://Join_(SQL)|SQL JOINs] to see the difference between those and which one is appropriate for your case.
